title: Ten seconds with a star

hosts.Leyla: lives in Baku and loves a good plan
hosts.Sam: grew up in Manchester and once travelled with no plan at all

before.predict: Have you ever met someone famous? Guess: who in this episode stood next to a famous actor — Leyla or Sam?

chapters.title: Coffee with a star
chapters.prompt: CHAPTER 1 SCENE: an airport coffee queue, a red-haired bearded man in a denim shirt looking nervous and excited next to a tall man in sunglasses and a cap, two photographers with big cameras and flashes behind a glass wall

chapters.title: Fifteen minutes of fame

chapters.title: A real role model

lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is famous people. And I have a celebrity story.
Oh, go on!
Two years ago, at the airport in London, I stood next to a very famous actor in the coffee queue. I won't say his name.
Did you say anything to him?
I said, "I'm a big fan." He said, "Thanks, mate." And that was it. Ten seconds.
[laugh] Still a great story. Were there paparazzi?
Two photographers, yes. They followed him all the way to the gate. He looked so tired.
I think that's the worst part of fame. No privacy at all. You can't even buy a coffee.
Exactly. Life in the limelight sounds fun, but every small mistake becomes news.
And one scandal can destroy your reputation in a day.
True. What about you, Leyla? Do you know anyone famous?
Sort of. A girl from my school posted a funny cooking video, and suddenly she had two million views.
Wow. Her fifteen minutes of fame!
[chuckle] More like fifteen days. Then people forgot. But she said it was enough for her.
Some people rise to fame slowly, over many years. I think that's healthier.
I agree. And I often think about who is a good role model for young people.
For me, it's not the most famous person. It's the person who does something useful with their fame.
Like a footballer who builds schools. That's a real legacy.
Yes. In fifty years nobody remembers the likes. They remember what you built.
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: if you could meet one famous person, who would it be — and what would you ask?
I'd ask that actor for eleven seconds. See you next time!
Bye for now!
